protections: Do-file content guard: GuardValidator runs the command/pattern blacklist over the text of the do-file before execution (src/stata_mcp/api/stata_do.py:78-96, src/stata_mcp/mcp_servers.py:211-240, src/stata_mcp/guard/validator.py:105-149); it never inspects the command script StataDo builds, nor the log name, nor the dofile path.

Do-file path boundary: the requested dofile path is resolve()d and must be relative_to STATA_MCP_FOLDER.DO or WORKING_DIR (src/stata_mcp/api/stata_do.py:22-30 and :51-76, src/stata_mcp/mcp_servers.py:183-208 and :532-540).

No OS shell on Unix: the Stata process is spawned with shell=False on Unix-like systems (src/stata_mcp/stata/stata_do/do.py:162-171 and :278-287); the Windows transport still uses shell=True with a hand-built batch path (do.py:225-232 and :360-368).
Log-name validation: none at the pinned commit - log_file_name is used verbatim as the log base name and interpolated into the `log using "..."` command text (do.py:81-82, :127-129, :175-181).
read_log directory boundary (src/stata_mcp/mcp_servers.py:471-489) exists but is a file-read control, not a command-construction control.

conflicts.what: A strict identifier rule for `help cmd` breaks a documented flow: on a successful install `_load_help_cls().help(package, replace=True)` is called with the package string (api/ado_install.py:54-58), and the documented GitHub form is `SepineTam/TexIV` (mcp_servers.py:328) - so the help validator must accept `/` to keep T5's own route working.

One shared allow-list cannot serve both parameters: log names must keep the all-digit `%Y%m%d%H%M%S` default (utils/__init__.py:11-12) and the dotted `analysis_wave1.dta` example (docs/api/overview.md:428), while package names need `/` and net sources need `:`/`/` inside `from(...)` (net_install.py:16-18, mcp_servers.py:371). A solver who refactors both through one validator breaks one of the two routes.

The natural Unix fix for the `do "..."` interpolation (shell-quote the path, reject backslashes/spaces) is wrong for the Windows transport, which interpolates a native `C:\...` path into the same quoted literal (do.py:220, :354); a fix that satisfies one transport changes behaviour on the other.

fairness_risks: The documented default log name is the `%Y%m%d%H%M%S` timestamp (utils/__init__.py:11-12): it starts with a digit, is all digits and is 14 characters. Any rule requiring a letter first, or forbidding all-digit names, breaks the default path.

The documented custom-name example is `log_file_name=f"analysis_{dataset}"` with dataset like `wave1.dta` (docs/api/overview.md:428), so dots must be allowed; the same string is returned to the caller as the log path, so a fix must not silently rewrite it.
Non-ASCII log names have no documented prohibition and the project ships Chinese docs (docs/api/overview.zh.md:128); rejecting non-ASCII would be an over-broad refusal of a legitimate shape.

Ado package installs legitimately use `user/repo` (mcp_servers.py:328) and `from(https://...)` URLs (github_install.py:30, mcp_servers.py:371), so a `no slashes/colons` rule for T5 refuses a documented input.

Absolute do-file paths with spaces are explicitly supported ('Paths with spaces now work correctly on Unix-like systems', CHANGELOG.md:572); a fix for T2 that rejects spaces or requires bare file names refuses a legitimate path shape.
Refusing over-long names (>128) has no documented support and no advisory basis; it is a plausible but arbitrary refusal.

design.why: Four independent judgements, each with a different reason to dismiss, spanning three packages. T1 is the report's own route and the cheap point, but it forces the fix-site decision: a regex added at one wrapper (api/stata_do.py:33 or mcp_servers.py:138) leaves the other two entry points and both transports open, while a check at do.py:81 closes the whole log-name group. T2 is the same function three lines below and looks already defended by the boundary check - the classic deepseek shape (protection appears to exist, a plausible dismissal exists) - and it survives any log-name-only fix. T4 is a second command-construction path one package away with a 'read-only documentation' alibi. T5 is a third, and it carries the coupled value (user/repo, from(URL)) that makes an over-broad shared validator break documented installs, i.e. the mimo failure. This beats designs built only on the do.py siblings: T1/T2/T3 all collapse if a solver validates both caller strings once at the top of execute_dofile, whereas the help and installer routes need separate decisions in separate modules. T3, T6 and T7 are kept as sub-routes of their groups (Windows transport, Windows installer branch, public builders) rather than separate judgements; T7 in particular is a lower-value injection room because no current entry point feeds it untrusted text.

No published fix diff or latest-release tree was available in this worktree, so every `present_in_latest` is unknown and the claim that the fix touches only do.py comes from the screener record, not from the patch itself.
The advisory text (GHSA-4P62-HQP5-G644 / CVE-2026-47708 / PYSEC-2026-544) was not read; the screener summary is treated as a lead.

Whether a behavioural hidden test can drive the pexpect routes (help, installers) on this host without a real Stata binary is untested; controller.py:99 is a plain sendline, so stubbing StataController and capturing the sent string looks feasible but was not run.
Whether the MCP `help` and `ado_package_install` tools are in the graded profile matters for reachability: both are registered in the 'all' profile and help is unix_only (mcp_servers.py:607-633).

Out-of-family sites deliberately excluded from the trap list: src/stata_mcp/api/read_log.py:26-32 has no directory boundary although mcp_servers.py:471-489 does, and get_data_info resolves arbitrary paths; both are file-read issues, not command construction.
